comment: Runtime registry for examples/customcmd. The program loads this file when it starts (and re-reads it as you type, so edits land immediately). Each entry declares ONE of your own scripts: its name, the command that runs it, a plain description of what it does, the argument slots it takes (in order, optional), a few example sentences in your own words (optional), and — for multi-step plans — an optional stage (inspect, prepare, execute, verify, cleanup), an optional after list naming scripts that should run first, and an optional acts_on hint (file, tests, repo, logs), and an optional needs list naming concepts that should run earlier in a plan. An entry may instead carry a steps list and no command: a named routine that expands into a plan of the commands its steps match. Adding your script means adding one entry here — there is NO retraining: the program matches what you type against these descriptions at runtime. See the README section 'Runnable example: your own commands, described not trained'. Some entries also state relations and an object_type: the typed relationships the command stands in (moves_from/moves_to on its from/to slots, requires on its needs) and the type of thing it acts on, which the relations layer validates seated values against; both are additive metadata the matcher ignores.
